data.summary: The routes directory is the HTTP/WebSocket API layer of this Rust/Axum backend, housing all route-group handlers for the workspace application. Each module owns one route group: buttons (register/remove user buttons), manifest (service manifest), preview (dynamic reverse proxy to dev servers), seam (reserved-API catch-all), stats (container resource snapshot), and terminal (pty WebSocket bridge). These handlers wire the axum router to AppState, config parsers, and infrastructure services, making this a hub of the backend's external surface.

file_insights.name: mod.rs
file_insights.summary: Module declaration file that exposes each route group (buttons, manifest, models, preview, seam, stats, terminal) as public submodules.
file_insights.source_summary: Contains only `pub mod` declarations for buttons, manifest, models, preview, seam, stats, and terminal. No executable logic; purely organizational.
file_insights.detailed_description: Serves as the aggregated re-export point for all route handler modules in the routes directory. It simply declares each submodule as public, giving the parent router access to every endpoint group handler.
responsibilities: Provide a single import surface for the routes layer

file_insights.name: buttons.rs
file_insights.summary: Handles POST/DELETE /api/buttons for registering and removing user-defined buttons persisted to buttons.toml, including validation, atomic writes, and live probe endpoints.
file_insights.source_summary: Defines ButtonInput/ButtonOut/ProbeQuery/ProbeOut structs plus slugify/unique_id helpers and write_buttons_atomic for crash-safe TOML persistence. Includes unit tests for slug generation, collision suffixing, type validation, and async tests probing live/dead ports.
file_insights.detailed_description: Implements the user-button CRUD API, writing atomically to the persistent workspace volume so registered buttons survive container restarts and are shared across browsers. It validates button types (agent/web), normalizes web ports, derives unique slugs/IDs, and exposes async probe handlers that test whether a port is live. Writes are serialized via AppState::file_lock.
responsibilities: Persist buttons.toml atomically under file lock
Probe whether web ports are listening

file_insights.name: manifest.rs
file_insights.summary: GET /api/manifest handler that builds a live service manifest per request by merging built-in and user buttons with availability checks.
file_insights.source_summary: Thin axum handler extracting State<AppState> and returning JSON from build_manifest, after loading/merging services and resolving button definitions via config functions.
file_insights.detailed_description: Computes the service manifest on each request so it reflects current availability: web-type entries via TCP reachability and agent-type entries via PATH existence. It merges built-in services.toml buttons with user buttons.toml, delegating to config helpers.

file_insights.name: preview.rs
file_insights.summary: Dynamic reverse proxy for /preview/<port>(/<path>) that forwards HTTP and WebSocket traffic to loopback-bound dev servers, including hop-by-hop header filtering.
file_insights.source_summary: Provides port_allowed, upstream_path, and is_hop_by_hop helpers with async proxying of Body/WebSocketUpgrade to 127.0.0.1:<port>. Includes tests covering port rejection, prefix stripping, and hop-by-hop header filtering.
file_insights.detailed_description: Implements a per-app reverse proxy so user-started dev servers (bound on the shared netns loopback) are reachable via /preview/<port>. It constructs upstream paths, blocks disallowed ports (zero/self), upgrades WebSockets, and strips RFC 7230 hop-by-hop headers when relaying responses.
responsibilities: Reverse-proxy HTTP requests to loopback dev servers

file_insights.name: seam.rs
file_insights.summary: Reserved-API catch-all handler returning 502 with a stub JSON body for /api, /v1, and /mcp prefixes until a future agent/SDK API exists.
file_insights.source_summary: Defines a single async seam handler returning (StatusCode, Json<Value>) with a stub payload; wired as a catch-all for reserved prefixes.
file_insights.detailed_description: Provides an explicit placeholder so reserved API surfaces (/api minus real endpoints, /v1, /mcp) are not swallowed by code-server or the static SPA. Wired as `any(seam)` on catch-all routes, it answers every method and sub-path with a 502 stub, proving the seam exists.
responsibilities: Answer all reserved-prefix requests with 502 stub
Reserve API namespace from being swallowed by other services

file_insights.name: stats.rs
file_insights.summary: GET /api/stats handler plus a background sampler that reports container-self CPU, memory, and disk usage for the statusbar footer.
file_insights.source_summary: Defines StatsSnapshot and stats/async handler, spawn_stats_sampler, read_cpu_usage_usec, effective_cpus, read_mem, and read_disk helpers reading cgroup v2 and statvfs data.
file_insights.detailed_description: Provides container-scoped resource metrics (not host) using cgroup v2 files for portability across host OSes. CPU% derives from cpu.stat usage_usec deltas over wall time against the effective CPU budget; memory and disk come from read_mem and statvfs. A spawn_stats_sampler periodically refreshes the shared StatsSnapshot.
responsibilities: Sample cgroup v2 CPU usage deltas

file_insights.name: terminal.rs
file_insights.summary: GET /api/term/ws WebSocket handler that spawns a pty (login shell or ?cmd= under it) and bidirectionally bridges it to the browser.
file_insights.source_summary: Defines TermQuery (cmd/cwd) and async terminal_ws plus run_pty_session, using axum WebSocketUpgrade, tokio mpsc, and spawn_pty with PtySize for the pty loop.
file_insights.detailed_description: Bridges a WebSocket to a spawned pty, routing client Text frames to pty stdin and pty stdout/stderr back to the client. Supports ?cmd= to run a command under a login shell and ?cwd= to override the working directory (falling back to /root). The pty runs as root since the app process does.
responsibilities: Bridge client keystrokes to pty stdin
Stream pty output back to client
